g.title: Benzoin condensation: Nucleophilic carbonyl addition
g.desc: Ph–CH=O + :CN− → PhCH(O−)CN. Cyanide carbon adds to aldehyde carbon; C=O pi electrons move to O.

g.text: Cyanide carbon adds to aldehyde carbon; C=O pi electrons move to O.

g.title: Benzoin condensation: Alkoxide protonation
g.desc: PhCH(O−)CN + H–solvent → PhCH(OH)CN + solvent−. The cyanohydrin alkoxide is protonated by the protic medium.

g.text: Condensed structural stage; electron changes are specified below.
The cyanohydrin alkoxide is protonated by the protic medium.

g.title: Benzoin condensation: Proton transfer
g.desc: Ph–C(OH)(CN)–H + :base → Ph–C−(OH)CN + H–base+. Deprotonation at the former aldehyde carbon forms the resonance-stabilized acyl-anion equivalent.

g.text: Deprotonation at the former aldehyde carbon forms the resonance-stabilized acyl-anion equivalent.

g.title: Benzoin condensation: Nucleophilic carbonyl addition
g.desc: Ph–C−(OH)CN + Ph–CH=O → PhC(OH)(CN)–CH(O−)Ph. The carbon nucleophile attacks a second benzaldehyde carbon.

g.text: The carbon nucleophile attacks a second benzaldehyde carbon.

g.title: Benzoin condensation: Internal proton inventory redistribution
g.desc: PhC(O–H)(CN)–CH(O−)Ph → PhC(O−)(CN)–CH(OH)Ph. A solvent-mediated proton relay transfers the original OH proton to the newly formed alkoxide; no free proton is implied.

g.text: Condensed structural stage; electron changes are specified below.

g.title: Benzoin condensation: Tetrahedral intermediate collapse
g.desc: Ph–C(O−)–CN attached to CH(OH)Ph → PhCOCH(OH)Ph + CN−. O forms C=O as the C–CN bond returns its pair to cyanide, regenerating catalyst.

g.text: O forms C=O as the C–CN bond returns its pair to cyanide, regenerating catalyst.
